rules.name: Geophysics Honors Program
rules.desc:
The department offers a program leading to a BS degree in Geophysics with honors. The honors program is open to students with a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.5 in all courses required for the Geophysics major and a minimum of 3.0 in all university coursework. The guidelines are:

• Select a research project, either theoretical, field, or experimental, that has the approval of an advisor.

• Submit a proposal to the department, which decides on its suitability as an honors project. Qualified students intending to pursue honors are encouraged to apply to the program during winter quarter of their junior year.

• The advisor assigns course credit for the project within the framework of the GEOPHYS 198 Honors Program.

• Whether a given independent study project merits an award of honors is made jointly by the department and the student’s advisor. This decision is based on the quality of the honors work and the student’s other work in Earth Sciences.

• The work done in the honors program cannot be used as a substitute for regularly required courses.

rules.name: Honors project approved and honors awarded by the department (GPA 3.5 in the major, 3.0 overall)

gpa: Declared majors must maintain a cumulative grade point average (GPA) of at least 2.0
grading: Students must earn a "C" or higher in all classes used for upper division elective requirement. All courses must be taken for a letter grade, unless only offered S/NC.
transferPolicy: Refer to university policy on Transfer Credit.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 62 units, the core, supporting math, physics and EPS courses, 6 units of GEOPHYS 196, 15 units of listed upper-level electives with a C or better, the Senior Seminar (GEOPHYS 199, the WIM course) and a capstone of GEOPHYS 197 or 198. Every course must be letter graded unless it is offered S/NC only. You check the 2.0 cumulative GPA yourself, and for honors the department approves the project and checks the honors GPA.
